newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe sees bumper 1997 wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe sees bumper 1997 wheat harvest.

text.p: Zimbabwe should harvest a record winter wheat crop this year following above average rains in most parts of the country, an industry official said.

Zimbabwe Cereal Producers Association chief executive Peter Wells told state news agency Ziana late on Wednesday that large amounts of water had flowed into dams and this year's wheat volumes were likely to exceed those for 1996, which tripled to 270,000 tonnes from 65,000 the previous year.
The crop is grown under irrigation in winter.
Wells added that some farmers might be discouraged from growing wheat because of previous hitches in marketing the cereal.
"Many growers are hesitant to grow more of the crop because of the marketing problems experienced last year," he said.
These included delays in getting export licences from the government, which were granted only after international wheat prices had plummeted.
"We are trying to restore confidence in the farmers and are currently conducting countrywide discussions to encourage them to grow more of the crop," Wells said.
